newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Metroplex in Reef Casino rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Metroplex in Reef Casino rescue plan.

text.p: Australian Tourism Group (ATG) said on Tuesday it has formed a rescue plan with Malaysian gaming group Metroplex Bhd for Reef Casino Trust, owner of Cairns casino in northern Queensland.

ATG said it and its associate Touraust Corp Pty Ltd and Sinophil Corp Inc, a unit of Metroplex, planned to form a joint venture to recapitalise Reef Casino, reorganise its operations and start new marketing strategies for the casino.
Under the proposal, Sinophil would make a major investment in the joint venture and inject a significant amount of capital into Reef Casino Trust, ATG said.

ATG said the proposal was presented by ATG and Touraust with the co-operation of Casinos Austria International Ltd, former manager of the Reef casino, following a tender process conducted by corporate advisers Grant Samuel & Associates.
A spokesman for ATG said it was likely that this proposal was the only one put forward under the tender process.

The proposal involves a rationalisation of existing lease and management structures, and is subject to a number of approvals including those of Reef Casino Trust unitholders, the trust's financiers and the Queensland government, ATG said.
The ATG/Touraust/Sinophil joint venture would control all operations of the Reef Hotel Casino complex through one chief executive officer, who will report to the joint venture company, ATG said.

The joint venture has also signed an agreement with Casinos Austria International to take control of the casino lease, while Touraust has agreed to sell its units in Reef Casino Trust and its hotel and entertainment leases to the joint venture in exchange for an interest in the venture.
ATG will also sell its units in Reef Casino Trust to the joint venture in exchange for an interest in the joint venture.

ATG, which is the operator of the Reef hotel in Cairns, has a 20 percent stake in Reef Casino Trust. The Australian Olympic Committee has eight percent, while Casino Austria International had 13 percent.
The Reef Casino Trust has being seeking a cash injection of around A$40 million since the end of 1996 to reduce its debt from A$105 million to about A$60 million.
In December, financiers withdrew a A$15 million external working capital facility used to fund high roller visits to the casino.
Trading in units in the Reef Casino Trust was suspended earlier on Tuesday pending an announcement on the financial restructure.
The units last traded at 14.5 cents last Thursday.
